inputs.prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] IMAGE-TO-VIDEO. ANIMATE THE PROVIDED INPUT IMAGE DIRECTLY. ABSOLUTE SUBJECT IDENTITY LOCK — HIGHEST PRIORITY. The two human subjects visible in the INPUT IMAGE are the ONLY human subjects allowed in this video. DO NOT generate new people. DO NOT replace either person. DO NOT reinterpret either person. DO NOT generate similar-looking substitutes. DO NOT recast the subjects. DO NOT reconstruct their identities. DO NOT create alternative faces. THIS IS NOT TEXT-TO-VIDEO. THIS IS NOT A NEW SCENE GENERATION. THIS IS DIRECT ANIMATION OF THE EXISTING INPUT PHOTOGRAPH. The exact man already visible on the LEFT side of the input image must remain the SAME man in every frame. The exact woman already visible on the RIGHT side of the input image must remain the SAME woman in every frame. Their faces from the input image are immutable identity anchors. Preserve EXACTLY: — same facial identity — same facial geometry — same eyes — same eye spacing — same eyebrows — same nose — same mouth — same teeth — same jawline — same cheeks — same ears — same skin tone — same apparent age — same hairstyle — same hairline — same hair color — same body proportions — same height relationship — same clothing — same accessories — same shoes ZERO CHARACTER REDESIGN. ZERO FACE REPLACEMENT. ZERO IDENTITY DRIFT. ZERO SUBJECT REGENERATION. Do not beautify the faces. Do not modify facial proportions. Do not make either person younger or older. Do not change ethnicity or skin characteristics. Do not change makeup. Do not change hairstyle. The first frame must be visually identical to the supplied input image. Treat the input photograph as a locked visual canvas. ANIMATION: Animate ONLY subtle motion already compatible with their existing poses. The man remains standing on the LEFT exactly where he is. Very subtle breathing. One natural blink. Tiny facial micro-expression while maintaining his existing smile. Extremely small natural head stabilization movement. The woman remains standing on the RIGHT exactly where she is. Very subtle breathing. One natural blink. Tiny facial micro-expression while maintaining her existing smile. Extremely small natural head stabilization movement. IMPORTANT: They continue looking generally toward the camera. DO NOT make them turn their heads significantly. DO NOT create profile views. DO NOT make them look strongly sideways. Do not require the model to invent facial information that is not visible in the source photograph. BODY: Preserve their original poses. No walking. No dancing. No repositioning. No hugging. No kissing. No hand gestures. No arm gestures. No body rotation. No pose changes. Keep hands and fingers stable. BACKGROUND: Preserve the EXACT floral environment from the input image. Do not regenerate the garden. Do not replace flowers. Do not change architecture. Do not introduce objects. Only extremely subtle natural leaf and flower movement from a gentle breeze. The woman's hair may have extremely subtle secondary movement. CAMERA: LOCKED CAMERA with an extremely subtle cinematic push-in. Maximum approximately 2–3% dolly-in throughout the entire shot. No orbit. No pan. No tilt. No camera shake. No reframing. No perspective change. No cuts. Keep BOTH complete bodies visible. Keep both heads and both pairs of shoes inside the frame. TEMPORAL CONSISTENCY: Every subsequent frame must remain geometrically and visually anchored to the original input frame. The source image determines identity. The source image determines anatomy. The source image determines clothing. The source image determines composition. The source image determines environment. Motion must adapt to the photograph. THE PHOTOGRAPH MUST NEVER ADAPT TO THE MOTION. If an intended motion would require changing facial identity, facial geometry, anatomy, clothing or appearance, REDUCE OR CANCEL THAT MOTION instead. IDENTITY PRESERVATION HAS PRIORITY OVER MOTION. NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS: new person, different man, different woman, replacement actor, replacement actress, similar person, new face, face replacement, face regeneration, face morphing, identity drift, identity interpolation, facial redesign, facial reconstruction, beautification, age change, skin change, hair change, body change, wardrobe change, character redesign, duplicate person, additional person, extra limbs, deformed hands, changing background, scene regeneration, camera orbit, head rotation, profile face, large movement. FINAL REQUIREMENT: The final video must unmistakably show THE EXACT SAME TWO PEOPLE FROM THE PROVIDED INPUT IMAGE. The desired result is the supplied photograph itself gently coming alive. Do not recreate the photograph. Do not recreate the people. ANIMATE THE EXISTING PEOPLE IN THE EXISTING PHOTOGRAPH.

overall_soundscape: Physical ambience and visible action sounds remain synchronized with the target video timeline.
